examples.en: People's minds were unsettled after they saw the news.
Don't get shaken so easily by a little rumor.

examples.ko: 시험 전날에는 마음이 동요돼서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The night before the exam I felt unsettled and couldn't sleep.
The teacher calmly soothed the students who were getting rattled.

examples.ko: 가격이 오른다는 말에 시장이 동요될 거예요.
examples.en: The market will probably get shaken by the talk of rising prices.

examples.ko: 그 말을 들은 팀원들은 크게 동요된 얼굴이었어요.
examples.en: The team members who heard that had greatly unsettled faces.

explain: '마음이 동요되다', '분위기가 동요되다'처럼 마음, 분위기, 시장 같은 말이 주어로 와요. 스스로 흔들리는 느낌이면 '동요하다'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 일상 대화에서는 '흔들리다'가 훨씬 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It usually takes things like a mind, a mood, or a market as its subject. When the person is the one wavering, 동요하다 works almost the same, but in everyday talk Koreans say 흔들리다 far more often.

examples.en: I don't waver at anything people say.

examples.ko: 결과를 기다리는 동안 마음이 자꾸 동요했어요.
examples.en: My mind kept wavering while I waited for the results.

examples.ko: 관객들이 동요하자 사회자가 조용히 해 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: When the audience got restless, the host asked for quiet.
The president reassured the people who were unsettled.

examples.ko: 그는 위기에도 동요하지 않고 침착하게 말했어요.
examples.en: Even in a crisis he spoke calmly without flinching.

examples.ko: 주가가 떨어지면 투자자들이 동요할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If stock prices fall, investors may get jittery.

explain: '동요하지 않다'처럼 부정형으로 가장 많이 써요. '침착하다', '흔들리지 않다'와 함께 나오는 일이 많고, 뉴스나 연설 같은 격식 있는 글에 자주 보여요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '흔들리다'나 '당황하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It shows up most often in the negative, 동요하지 않다. It pairs with words like 침착하다 and appears more in news and speeches. With friends, 흔들리다 or 당황하다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: Trains run on rails.
The curtain rail came off, so I put it back up.

examples.ko: 공사 때문에 레일을 새로 깔고 있어요.
examples.en: They are laying new rails because of construction.

examples.ko: 서랍 레일이 고장 나서 잘 안 열려요.
examples.en: The drawer rail is broken, so it doesn't open well.

examples.ko: 아이들이 장난감 기차 레일을 길게 이었어요.
examples.en: The kids connected the toy train rails into a long line.
I want to install track lighting on the ceiling.

explain: 기차 선로만이 아니라 커튼, 서랍, 조명처럼 무언가가 미끄러져 움직이는 길에도 써요. 기차 선로는 '철로'나 '선로'라고도 해요. 영어 rail에서 온 말이라 '레일 바이크'처럼 다른 말과 붙어 쓰이는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: Beyond train tracks, it covers any guide that something slides along, like curtains, drawers, or lights. For train tracks, 철로 and 선로 are also common. It often attaches to other words, as in 레일 바이크.

examples.en: My passport expires next month.
The transit card's validity period expired yesterday.
Please contact me before the contract expires.

examples.ko: 쿠폰 유효기간이 만료돼서 쓸 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The coupon had expired, so I couldn't use it.
You can't pay with an expired card.

examples.ko: 이 이용권은 올해 말에 만료될 거예요.
examples.en: This pass will expire at the end of this year.

explain: 기간이 정해진 것(여권, 계약, 카드, 쿠폰)이 끝날 때 써요. 같은 일을 사람이 주어로 말하면 '만료하다'를 쓰는데 훨씬 드물어요.
explain_en: Use it for things with a set period, such as passports, contracts, cards, and coupons. 만료하다, with a person as the subject, is much rarer.

examples.en: The CEO will complete his term at the end of this year.
After serving out his term, a new CEO came in.
He completed his service period and was discharged.
A man who completed his sentence was released today.
Once the contract period ends, the rate changes.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 전속 계약을 만료하고 새 회사로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: The singer finished his exclusive contract and moved to a new company.

explain: '임기를 만료하다', '형기를 만료하다'처럼 주로 공문서와 뉴스에서 써요. 일상에서는 '만료되다'나 '끝나다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 목적어를 받는 타동사로 쓰면 '기간을 다 채우고 끝내다'라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It appears mostly in official documents and news, as in 임기를 만료하다 and 형기를 만료하다. In daily speech 만료되다 or 끝나다 is more natural. Used transitively, it carries a sense of finishing out the full period.

examples.en: That writer won a literary award this year.
I bought the award-winning book at the bookstore.
Our school gives a literary award to students every year.

examples.ko: 제 꿈은 신인 문학상에 당선되는 거예요.
examples.en: My dream is to win a new writers' literary award.

examples.ko: 문학상 후보에 오른 소설을 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm reading a novel nominated for the literary award.

examples.ko: 이번 문학상은 시 부문 심사가 어려웠대요.
examples.en: I heard judging the poetry category was hard for this award.

explain: '문학상을 받다', '문학상에 당선되다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 달라요. '노벨 문학상'처럼 이름 앞에 붙여서 말해요. 시, 소설 같은 글을 쓰는 사람이 받는 상이에요.
explain_en: The verbs change with context: 문학상을 받다 for receiving it, 문학상에 당선되다 for winning a contest. It attaches to names, as in 노벨 문학상. It is given to people who write poetry, fiction, and similar works.

examples.en: I study law at university.

examples.ko: 법학 수업은 읽을 자료가 아주 많아요.
examples.en: Law classes have a lot of reading material.
My older sister plans to go to law school.
Many people who majored in law applied.
That professor is famous in the field of law.
I got interested in law, so I bought a book.

explain: 법을 연구하는 학문이라서 '법학과', '법학 박사', '법학을 전공하다'처럼 학문과 학교 이야기에서 써요. 법 자체는 '법', 법률 일을 하는 사람은 '변호사', '판사'라고 해요. '법학'은 법을 공부하고 연구하는 분야를, '법률'은 나라가 정한 규칙을 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is the academic study of law, used in phrases like 법학과, 법학 박사 and 법학을 전공하다. The law itself is 법, and legal professionals are 변호사 or 판사. 법학 is the field of studying and researching law, while 법률 refers to the rules a country sets.

examples.en: The defendant entered the court with his lawyer.
The defense counsel argued for innocence.

examples.ko: 경찰은 조사 전에 변호인을 부를 수 있다고 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The police said he could call counsel before questioning.
The defense side submitted new evidence.

examples.ko: 그는 믿을 만한 변호인을 구하고 있어요.
examples.en: He is looking for a trustworthy lawyer.
I heard the defense counsel's statement on the news.

explain: 재판이나 수사에서 피고인 편에서 돕는 사람을 가리켜요. 일반적으로 법률 일을 하는 직업은 '변호사'라고 해요. 같은 사람이어도 사건 안에서의 역할을 말하면 '변호인', 직업을 말하면 '변호사'예요.
explain_en: It refers to the person who stands with the accused during a trial or investigation. The profession is 변호사. The same person is 변호인 when you talk about the role in a case, and 변호사 when you talk about the job.

examples.en: When you're stressed, hormone secretion increases.

examples.ko: 침 분비가 줄면 입이 마르는 느낌이 들어요.
examples.en: When saliva secretion drops, your mouth feels dry.
If you exercise, you secrete more sweat.

examples.ko: 위산 분비가 많으면 속이 쓰릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Too much stomach acid secretion can cause heartburn.

examples.ko: 잠을 못 자면 호르몬 분비에 문제가 생겨요.
examples.en: If you can't sleep, problems occur in hormone secretion.

examples.ko: 이 약은 땀 분비를 막아 줘요.
examples.en: This medicine blocks sweat secretion.

explain: 몸에서 침, 땀, 호르몬 같은 물질이 나오는 일을 말할 때 써요. 과학, 건강 이야기에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '땀이 나다'처럼 더 쉬운 말을 써요. '호르몬 분비', '침 분비'처럼 나오는 물질 이름 뒤에 붙여요.
explain_en: Used for the body releasing substances like saliva, sweat, or hormones. It turns up in science and health talk, while everyday speech uses simpler phrasing such as 땀이 나다. It attaches after the substance, as in 호르몬 분비.

examples.en: The body secretes a sleep hormone at night.
The salivary gland is where saliva is secreted.

examples.ko: 식물이 이상한 냄새를 분비해서 벌레를 쫓아요.
examples.en: The plant secretes a strange smell to keep bugs away.
My body released adrenaline when I got nervous.

examples.ko: 이 세포는 독소를 분비할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This cell can secrete toxins.

examples.ko: 위가 위산을 너무 많이 분비하면 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts when the stomach secretes too much acid.

explain: 몸이나 식물이 어떤 물질을 안에서 밖으로 내보낼 때 써요. 과학 수업이나 건강 정보에서 나오는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않아요. '땀을 흘리다', '침이 나오다'처럼 쉬운 표현을 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: Used when a body or plant releases a substance from inside. It belongs to science class and health info, and is almost never used in casual talk, where phrases like 땀을 흘리다 or 침이 나오다 are more common.

examples.en: Children pick up new languages quickly.
It takes time to acquire this skill.
I acquired Korean while living in Korea.

examples.ko: 길에서 지갑을 습득한 사람은 경찰서에 가져다주세요.
examples.en: If you find a wallet on the street, please take it to the police station.
Acquiring new knowledge is fun.
He picked up driving skills easily.

explain: 언어나 기술은 공부와 경험으로 천천히 몸에 익힐 때 써요. 그리고 '분실물 습득'처럼 잃어버린 물건을 주웠을 때도 써요. 일상 대화에서 기술을 말할 때는 '배우다', '익히다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: For languages and skills, it means gradually making them your own through study and experience. It is also used for finding lost items, as in 분실물 습득. In daily conversation 배우다 or 익히다 sounds more natural for skills.

examples.en: My parents agreed to my studying abroad.
The boss approved my vacation request.
She gladly agreed to my request.
After thinking about it for a long time, I decided to agree.

examples.ko: 그는 결혼 제안을 승낙할 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems he will accept the marriage proposal.

examples.ko: 제가 먼저 부탁했는데 상대방이 승낙하지 않았어요.
examples.en: I asked first, but the other person didn't consent.

explain: '허락하다'와 비슷하지만 '승낙하다'는 부탁이나 요청을 받아들여 '좋다'고 답한다는 느낌이 강해요. 윗사람이나 회사처럼 결정하는 쪽의 대답으로 자주 나와요. 친구끼리는 보통 '좋아', '그래'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Close to 허락하다, but 승낙하다 stresses accepting a request and answering yes. It often describes the reply from someone with the authority to decide, like a boss or company. Between friends people just say 좋아 or 그래.

examples.en: The police questioning went on until late at night.

examples.ko: 그는 심문을 받는 동안 한마디도 안 했어요.
examples.en: He didn't say a word while being interrogated.
The judge started questioning the witness.
The interrogation scene was the scariest part of the movie.
The questioning process is being recorded.

examples.ko: 긴 심문 끝에 범인이 입을 열었어요.
examples.en: After a long interrogation, the criminal finally spoke.

explain: 경찰이나 법원이 사건과 관련된 사람에게 캐묻는 일이에요. 일상의 '질문하다'나 '묻다'와 달리 압박하는 느낌이 있어서, 친구에게 뭔가 계속 물을 때는 쓰지 않아요. 같은 뜻의 '취조'는 주로 경찰이 할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is when police or a court press someone about a case. Unlike plain 질문하다 or 묻다, it carries pressure, so you wouldn't use it for friends asking questions. 취조 is a close word used mostly for police questioning.

examples.en: The police interrogated the suspect.
I saw a scene where a judge questions a witness.

examples.ko: 형사는 밤새 그 사람을 심문했지만 답을 못 얻었어요.
examples.en: The detective questioned him all night but got no answer.
Don't ask me questions as if you're interrogating me.
The prosecutor will question the defendant tomorrow.
My mom grilled me for telling a lie.

explain: 법적인 상황에서 캐묻는다는 뜻이라 일상에서는 농담처럼 '나를 심문하지 마'라고 쓰기도 해요. 사실을 확인하려고 계속 물을 때 장난스럽게 쓰는 거예요. 평소에 묻는 건 '묻다', '물어보다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a legal-setting word, but people jokingly say 나를 심문하지 마 when someone keeps pressing them. For ordinary asking, use 묻다 or 물어보다.

examples.en: Life is finite, so it is even more precious.
The Earth's resources are limited.
Time is limited, so let's start with the important things.

examples.ko: 우리의 에너지는 유한한데 할 일은 너무 많아요.
examples.en: Our energy is limited, but there is too much to do.
We have to hold the event on a limited budget.

examples.ko: 모든 생명이 유한하다는 걸 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: I came to realize that all life is finite.

explain: 반의어는 '무한하다'예요. 시간, 자원, 생명처럼 끝이 있는 것을 말할 때 쓰고, 철학이나 과학, 논설문에서 자주 나와요. 일상에서 '시간이 별로 없다'는 말은 '시간이 부족하다'가 더 흔해요.
explain_en: The opposite is 무한하다. It describes things with an end, such as time, resources, and life, and appears often in philosophy, science, and essays. In daily talk, 시간이 부족하다 is more common than saying time is 유한하다.

examples.ko: 그는 자진 신고를 해서 벌이 줄었어요.
examples.en: He turned himself in voluntarily, so his penalty was reduced.
He announced his intention to resign of his own accord.
The voluntary payment period lasts until next week.
I took on the cleaning of my own accord.
No one stepped forward voluntarily.

examples.ko: 이 일은 자진 참여하는 사람만 하면 돼요.
examples.en: Only people who join voluntarily need to do this.

explain: '자진 신고', '자진 퇴사', '자진 납부'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 시키지 않아도 스스로 한다는 뜻을 더해요. 일상에서 '자원하다'나 '스스로'도 비슷하게 쓰지만, '자진'은 신고, 퇴사, 납부 같은 공식적인 일에 특히 많이 어울려요.
explain_en: It often attaches before another word, as in 자진 신고, 자진 퇴사, and 자진 납부, to show something was done without being told. 스스로 is similar in daily speech, but 자진 fits especially well with formal matters like reporting, resigning, or paying.

en: volunteer; do of one's own accord

examples.en: I volunteered to do the presentation.
The culprit came to the police station of his own accord.

examples.ko: 아무도 자진해 나서지 않아서 제비뽑기를 했어요.
examples.en: Nobody stepped forward, so we drew lots.
He took responsibility of his own accord.
We decided to give a prize to those who volunteer.
I was grateful that my coworker offered to help.

explain: 거의 '자진해서' 모양으로 써요. 누가 시키지 않았는데 스스로 나선다는 느낌이에요. '자원하다'는 일이나 봉사에 나설 때 쓰고, '자진해서'는 발표, 신고, 사과, 책임처럼 폭넓게 어울려요. 명사 '자진'은 '자진 신고'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어요.
explain_en: It appears almost always as 자진해서, meaning stepping up without being told. 자원하다 is for volunteering for work or service, while 자진해서 fits a wider range, such as a presentation, reporting, apologizing or taking responsibility. The noun 자진 attaches before another word, as in 자진 신고.

en: watch closely; keep an eye on

examples.en: Everyone is closely watching the election results.
The police kept an eye on the suspect's movements.
Many people are watching exchange rate changes closely.
I will keep watching the situation from now on.
The teacher gazed steadily at me.
Experts watch the market and prepare a response.

explain: 눈으로 뚫어지게 본다는 느낌과 함께 '앞으로 어떻게 되는지 지켜본다'는 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스에서 '결과를 주시하다', '상황을 주시하다'로 아주 자주 나와요. 친구 사이에서는 '지켜보다'나 '쳐다보다'가 더 편해요.
explain_en: It combines staring intently with watching to see how things turn out. News uses 결과를 주시하다 and 상황을 주시하다 constantly. Among friends, 지켜보다 or 쳐다보다 feels more comfortable.

examples.en: He raised his hand without hesitation.
There was no time to hesitate, so I dove right in.

examples.ko: 잠깐의 주저 끝에 그는 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: After a moment's hesitation, he opened the door.
I could sense hesitation in her voice.
Don't hesitate to ask whatever you're curious about.
I hesitated a lot before making the decision.

explain: '주저 없이', '주저하지 말고'처럼 거의 정해진 모양으로 많이 써요. 특히 '주저하지 말고 연락 주세요'는 편지나 안내문에서 정중하게 부탁할 때 자주 나와요. 말로는 '망설이지 말고'가 더 부드러워요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in set patterns like 주저 없이 and 주저하지 말고. 주저하지 말고 연락 주세요 is a very common polite line in letters and notices. In speech, 망설이지 말고 sounds softer.

examples.en: I hesitated for a moment before the presentation.
If you're curious about something, don't hesitate.
He seemed reluctant to apologize.
If you hesitate too long, you'll miss the chance.
She told the truth without hesitating.

examples.ko: 아이는 낯선 사람 앞에서 주저하다가 숨었어요.
examples.en: The child hesitated in front of a stranger and then hid.

explain: '망설이다'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만, '주저하다'가 더 글 같고 격식 있는 느낌이에요. '주저하지 마세요'는 안내문과 이메일에서, '망설이지 마세요'는 말할 때 더 자주 써요. 주로 부정형으로 나와요.
explain_en: Almost the same as 망설이다, but 주저하다 sounds more written and formal. 주저하지 마세요 fits notices and emails, while 망설이지 마세요 is more common in speech. It mostly appears in the negative.

examples.en: The car body was badly dented in the accident.

examples.ko: 이 차는 차체가 가벼워서 연비가 좋아요.
examples.en: This car has a light body, so the fuel economy is good.
The shop repainted the car body.
A scratch mark appeared on the car body.
The bus body is long, so turning is difficult.
Electric cars have the battery under the car body.

explain: 자동차에서 엔진, 바퀴, 의자를 뺀 겉 몸체를 말할 때 써요. 정비소나 자동차 설명에서 '차체 수리', '차체 무게'로 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 그냥 '차'라고 하지만 정비나 판매 이야기에서는 '차체'를 구분해서 말해요.
explain_en: It means the main body shell of a car, apart from the engine, wheels, and seats. You hear it at repair shops and in car specs, as in 차체 수리 and 차체 무게. In daily talk people just say 차, but 차체 is separated out for repairs and sales.

examples.en: I compared prices with other companies' products.
Our company's service is faster than other companies'.
Someone who moved from another company became team leader.
I got an idea from another company's ad.

examples.ko: 이 쿠폰은 타사 제품에는 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: This coupon can't be used on other companies' products.
Projects with other companies have increased.

explain: '우리 회사'가 아닌 다른 회사를 가리킬 때 써요. 회사 안에서 '타사 제품', '타사 대비'처럼 비교하는 말에서 자주 나와요. 반대로 우리 회사는 '자사'라고 해요. 둘이 짝이라서 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It points to a company other than your own, and often appears in comparisons like 타사 제품 and 타사 대비. The opposite, meaning your own company, is 자사. They come as a pair, so it helps to learn them together.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 요리 특화 교육으로 유명해요.
examples.en: This school is famous for its cooking-specialized education.

examples.ko: 회사는 어린이 제품 특화 전략을 세웠어요.
examples.en: The company set a strategy to specialize in kids' products.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 여행 정보에 특화되어 있어요.
examples.en: This app is specialized in travel information.

examples.ko: 저희 가게는 매운 국수에 특화된 곳이에요.
examples.en: Our shop specializes in spicy noodles.

examples.ko: 지역 특화 산업을 키우는 일이 중요해요.
examples.en: Developing regional specialized industries is important.
You need a specialized skill to survive the competition.

explain: 한 분야에 집중해서 강하게 만든다는 느낌이라 '특화 서비스', '특화 전략'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 써요. '전문'과 비슷하지만 '전문'은 사람이나 가게가 잘하는 분야를, '특화'는 제품이나 서비스를 그 방향으로 맞췄다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of focusing on one area to make it strong, and attaches before another word, as in 특화 서비스 and 특화 전략. Close to 전문, but 전문 is about what a person or shop is good at, while 특화 leans toward a product or service being tailored that way.

examples.en: Water is a compound made of hydrogen and oxygen.

examples.ko: 화합물은 두 가지 이상의 원소가 합쳐진 거예요.
examples.en: A compound is made of two or more elements joined together.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 화합물과 혼합물의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In science class I learned the difference between compounds and mixtures.

examples.ko: 이 화합물은 불에 타면 독가스가 나와요.
examples.en: This compound gives off toxic gas when burned.
The researcher created a new compound.
Salt is also one of the compounds.

explain: 과학 용어라서 화학 수업과 뉴스 기사에서 써요. 한 가지 원소로만 된 '원소'나 여러 물질이 그냥 섞인 '혼합물'과 구별해서 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 나오지 않아요.
explain_en: A science term for chemistry class and news articles. It is distinguished from 원소 (single element) and 혼합물 (a mere mixture). It almost never comes up in daily conversation.

examples.en: I fell on the stairs and broke my leg.
The doctor looked at the X-ray and said it was a fracture.

examples.ko: 골절 수술을 받고 한 달 동안 입원했어요.
examples.en: I had fracture surgery and stayed in the hospital for a month.
As you get older, the risk of fracture grows.
I broke my wrist while skiing.
It takes time for a fractured bone to heal.

explain: 병원에서 쓰는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '뼈가 부러지다'나 '다리가 부러졌다'고 훨씬 더 자주 말해요. 병원 안내나 뉴스에서는 '골절상'이라는 말도 나와요.
explain_en: A hospital word. In daily speech Koreans say 뼈가 부러지다 or 다리가 부러졌다 much more often. In hospital notices and the news you may also see 골절상.

examples.en: Don't say things like that.
There's no need to get mad over something like that.
I don't want to hear an excuse like that.
Why did you buy something like that?
Don't believe a rumor like that.
Stop thinking that kind of thought.

explain: '그런'과 비슷하지만 말하는 사람이 그것을 하찮게 보거나 못마땅해하는 느낌이 들어요. 그래서 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. 비슷한 말로 '이딴', '저딴'이 있고, 가까운 사이에서 화나거나 가볍게 말할 때 나와요.
explain_en: Like 그런, but it sounds dismissive or disapproving, so don't use it with elders or people you just met. 이딴 and 저딴 are the same pattern, and you hear them among close friends when someone is annoyed or casual.

examples.en: The chair's screw came loose, so it wobbles.
Please turn the screw with a screwdriver and tighten it.
I lost one small screw.
The screw in my glasses fell out, so I went to the optician.

examples.ko: 책상을 조립하려고 나사를 열 개 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought ten screws to assemble the desk.
This screw is too short.

explain: '나사를 조이다', '나사를 풀다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 정해져 있어요. '못'은 망치로 박지만, '나사'는 돌려서 박는 것이라 구별돼요. 드라이버로 돌리는 도구는 '드라이버'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 요즘 팀 분위기에 나사가 풀린 것 같아요.
phrases.en: to get slack; to lose focus
phrases.nuance_ko: 나사가 풀린 기계처럼 사람이나 분위기가 느슨해지고 정신을 놓았다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like a machine whose screw has come loose, a person or mood has become slack and lost focus.

explain_en: The verbs are set: 나사를 조이다 (tighten) and 나사를 풀다 (loosen). 못 (nail) is hammered in, while 나사 is turned in. The tool you turn it with is a 드라이버 (screwdriver).

examples.en: There is a formal dinner at the embassy tonight.
The two countries' representatives shared a banquet.
Korean food was served on the banquet menu.
We held a small formal dinner with just family.

examples.ko: 결혼 전날에 친구들이 만찬을 준비해 줬어요.
examples.en: The day before the wedding, my friends prepared a feast for me.

examples.ko: 그 만찬에는 옷을 차려입고 가야 해요.
examples.en: You have to dress up for that dinner.

explain: 특별한 손님이나 행사를 위해 차린 격식 있는 저녁 식사를 말해요. 평소 저녁밥은 '저녁'이나 '저녁 식사'라고 해요. 뉴스에서 정상 회담 뒤의 '공식 만찬'으로 아주 자주 나오고, 집에서 일상적으로 쓰는 말은 아니에요.
explain_en: A formal evening meal laid out for special guests or events. A normal dinner is 저녁 or 저녁 식사. In news it appears constantly as 공식 만찬 after summits, and it is not an everyday home word.

examples.en: This area is a densely populated region.

examples.ko: 건물이 밀집한 곳에서는 불이 나면 위험해요.
examples.en: If a fire breaks out where buildings are packed together, it is dangerous.

examples.ko: 밀집 상태가 심해서 지하철이 너무 불편해요.
examples.en: The crowding is so severe that the subway is very uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 공장이 밀집해 있어서 공기가 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Factories are clustered here, so the air is bad.
I had lunch on a street packed with restaurants.
The players bunched up in front of the goal and blocked.

explain: 사람이나 건물, 가게가 한곳에 빽빽하게 모여 있다는 느낌이에요. '인구 밀집', '상가 밀집'처럼 다른 말과 붙어 쓰는 일이 많아요. 일상에서 사람이 붐빌 때는 '붐비다', '북적이다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It suggests people, buildings, or shops packed tightly into one spot. It often joins other words, as in 인구 밀집 and 상가 밀집. For a crowded place in daily speech, 붐비다 or 북적이다 is far more natural.

examples.en: Tourists are concentrated in the city center.

examples.ko: 병원이 한 건물에 밀집돼서 찾기 쉬워요.
examples.en: Clinics are grouped in one building, so they are easy to find.
On weekends, people crowd into the park.

examples.ko: 대학교 근처에 원룸이 밀집된 동네가 있어요.
examples.en: Near the university there is a neighborhood packed with studio apartments.

examples.ko: 학원이 밀집되어 있는 거리에는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many students on streets where academies are clustered.
The more the population concentrates, the more housing prices rise.

explain: '밀집하다'는 스스로 모여 있는 모습을, '밀집되다'는 어떤 이유로 한곳에 모이게 된 결과를 말하는 느낌이에요. 실제 말에서는 두 표현이 거의 바꿔 쓰여요. 보통 '~에 밀집돼 있다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: 밀집하다 describes things gathering on their own, while 밀집되다 describes the result of being gathered somewhere for some reason. In practice the two swap freely. It is usually used as ~에 밀집돼 있다.

examples.en: Teenagers sometimes rebel against their parents.
That child defied the teacher.
The mother is worried because of her defiant son.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때 이유 없이 반항했어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I rebelled for no reason.
I thought it was useless to rebel.
It's a movie where the main character rebels against society.

explain: '부모님께 반항하다', '선생님께 반항하다'처럼 윗사람의 말을 따르지 않고 맞서는 일에 써요. '반대하다'는 의견이 다르다는 뜻이고, '반항하다'는 태도나 행동으로 대드는 느낌이 더 강해요. 같은 뜻의 명사 '반항'은 '반항기'처럼 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used for pushing back against authority, as in 부모님께 반항하다. 반대하다 only means disagreeing, whereas 반항하다 is more about attitude and behavior that talks back. The noun 반항 also appears in words like 반항기 (rebellious phase).

examples.en: After graduating, I drifted aimlessly for a while.
I lost my way and wandered around the alley.
It's a novel about wandering youth.
I'm struggling a lot over my career path.

examples.ko: 너무 오래 방황하지 말고 방향을 정해요.
examples.en: Don't wander for too long, and decide on a direction.
He, who had been drifting, finally found his dream.

explain: 길을 잃고 헤매는 모습도 말하지만, 요즘은 인생 방향을 못 찾고 마음이 흔들리는 시기에 더 자주 써요. '방황의 시기', '방황을 끝내다'처럼 시기와 같이 나와요. 단순히 길을 헤맬 때는 '헤매다'가 더 일상적이에요.
explain_en: It can mean losing your way physically, but today it is used more for a period of feeling lost about your life direction, as in 방황의 시기. For simply getting lost on the road, 헤매다 is more everyday.

examples.en: The witch in the fairy tale laughed wickedly.
The villain in that movie is truly evil.
A wicked thought flashed through my mind.
I felt that person was wicked.
The wicked-looking expression scared me.
The king was fooled by an evil wizard.

explain: '나쁘다'보다 훨씬 강하고, 마음이 일부러 못되고 해로운 쪽이라는 느낌이에요. 주로 동화, 영화, 소설 속 악당을 말할 때 나와요. 실제로 사람을 평가할 때는 '못됐다', '악하다'가 더 흔해서, '사악하다'를 쓰면 꽤 과장되게 들려요.
explain_en: Much stronger than 나쁘다, suggesting a deliberately cruel, harmful heart. It mostly shows up for villains in fairy tales, movies, and novels. For real people, 못됐다 or 악하다 is more common, and 사악하다 sounds quite dramatic.

examples.en: The colors in this photo are really pretty.
That painter has an excellent sense of color.
I bought a bag in warm tones.
If you use a filter, the color tone changes.
In interior design, matching the color tones is important.

examples.ko: 저는 이 그림의 색감이 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like the color feel of this painting.

explain: 색 자체가 아니라 색이 주는 전체 느낌과 분위기를 말해요. 그래서 '빨간색'보다는 '따뜻한 색감', '차분한 색감'처럼 말해요. 사진, 그림, 옷, 인테리어를 평가할 때 일상에서도 자주 써요. 비슷한 말 '색깔'은 그냥 어떤 색인지를 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the overall feel and mood that colors give, not the color itself, so Koreans say 따뜻한 색감 or 차분한 색감 rather than just red. It is common in daily talk about photos, paintings, clothes, and interiors. 색깔 simply tells which color it is.

examples.en: The court decided to imprison the criminal.
The police temporarily detained the suspect.

examples.ko: 교도소는 죄를 지은 사람을 수감하는 곳이에요.
examples.en: A prison is a place that holds people who committed crimes.

examples.ko: 서류 절차 때문에 범인을 수감하는 데 하루가 더 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Because of the paperwork, it took one more day to put the criminal in prison.
They will put him in prison right after the trial ends.
They do a health check before imprisoning someone.

explain: 교도소나 구치소에 가둔다는 법적인 말이에요. 수감하는 주체는 법원이나 경찰 같은 기관이고, 갇히는 사람 입장에서는 '수감되다'를 써요. 뉴스에서 '교도소에 수감 중'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A legal word for putting someone in a prison or detention center. The one doing it is an institution like a court or the police, and from the prisoner's side you say 수감되다. News often uses 교도소에 수감 중.

examples.en: The child sits quietly and draws.
The puppy is waiting patiently.
You need to behave during class.

examples.ko: 동생은 손님이 오면 갑자기 얌전히 굴어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling suddenly behaves well when guests come.
The doctor told me to rest quietly at home.
She greeted politely and took her seat.

explain: 조용하고 점잖게 행동하는 모습에 써요. 아이나 동물에게 가장 많이 쓰고, '얌전히 있어'는 가만히 조용히 있으라고 할 때 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 '조용한 성격'이라는 칭찬이 될 수도 있고, 답답하다는 느낌도 줄 수 있어요.
explain_en: Used for behaving in a quiet, well-mannered way, most often with children and animals. 얌전히 있어 means stay quiet and behave. For adults it can praise a calm personality, or hint that someone is too stiff.

en: accomplish; carry out to the end

examples.en: I completed the work I was assigned to the end.
I really want to accomplish this mission.

examples.ko: 선수들은 목표를 완수하기 위해 열심히 훈련해요.
examples.en: The players train hard to achieve their goal.
If you complete the task you promised, you get a reward.

examples.ko: 그는 어려운 과제를 완수한 뒤 휴가를 떠났어요.
examples.en: He went on vacation after completing the hard assignment.
I'm confident I can see it through to the end.

explain: '끝내다'보다 책임이나 임무를 끝까지 해냈다는 무게가 있어요. '임무를 완수하다', '목표를 완수하다'처럼 목적어가 임무, 책임, 목표인 경우가 많아요. 가벼운 일에는 '다 하다', '끝내다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Heavier than 끝내다, it carries the weight of seeing a duty or mission through to the end. Its objects are often 임무, 책임, or 목표. For light tasks, 다 하다 or 끝내다 is more natural.

examples.en: I switched to the business department in my second year.
To change your major, you need good grades.

examples.ko: 친구가 적성에 안 맞아서 전과하고 싶대요.
examples.en: My friend says he wants to switch majors because it doesn't suit him.

examples.ko: 전과한 뒤에는 새로 배울 게 많았어요.
examples.en: After I switched majors, there was a lot of new material to learn.
My older sister will switch from medicine to law.

examples.ko: 전과하는 학생은 학기 초에 신청해야 해요.
examples.en: Students who transfer departments must apply at the start of the semester.

explain: 대학교에서 다니던 학과를 다른 학과로 바꾸는 일을 말해요. 학교에서만 쓰는 말이라서 '과를 바꾸다'로도 말해요. 비슷하지만 '전공을 바꾸다'는 공부 분야 자체를 바꾼다는 느낌이고, '전과'는 학교에 정식으로 신청하는 절차라는 느낌이 있어요. 같은 소리의 '전과'(범죄 기록)와는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It means switching from one university department to another. You can also say 과를 바꾸다. 전공을 바꾸다 stresses changing the field of study, while 전과하다 feels like the official application process. Do not confuse it with 전과 meaning a criminal record, which is a different word.

examples.ko: 저는 학교 다닐 때 선배를 오래 짝사랑했어요.
examples.en: When I was in school, I had a long one-sided crush on a senior.
Many people have a secret crush on that friend.
I finally confessed to the person I had been secretly loving.
Loving someone one-sidedly hurts.
My friends noticed that I had a one-sided crush.

examples.ko: 그 드라마 주인공은 친구를 십 년 동안 짝사랑해요.
examples.en: The main character in that drama has loved his friend one-sidedly for ten years.

explain: 상대는 모르거나 받아 주지 않는데 나만 좋아하는 마음이에요. 명사 '짝사랑'도 같이 써요. 서로 좋아하는 사이는 '서로 사랑하다'나 '사귀다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Loving someone who doesn't know or doesn't return it. The noun 짝사랑 is used too. For feelings shared by both people, say 서로 사랑하다 or 사귀다 (to go out).

examples.en: I warmly hugged the friend I hadn't seen in ages.
I cried hugging my family at the airport.
The winning players hugged each other.

explain: '안다'와 뜻은 비슷하지만 '포옹하다'는 서로 껴안는 장면을 글처럼 말하는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '안아 주다', '안기다', '껴안다'가 더 자연스러워요. 뉴스나 소설, 영화 설명에서는 '포옹하다'가 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Similar to 안다, but 포옹하다 reads like describing a hugging scene in writing. In daily talk, 안아 주다, 안기다, or 껴안다 is more natural. News, novels, and film descriptions use 포옹하다 often.
